description:
## Goal

Make `boolean` the sole source-level builtin type constructor, matching Elixir typespecs.

## Observed state

`src/compiler2/resolve.rs` registers `bool`; `boolean` is currently an unknown type name. The maintained `.fz` library uses `bool` in 70 `@spec` and extern annotations, so a registry-only rename would leave the runtime prelude unresolved. `.agent/docs/type-naming.md` documents the old spelling.

## Scope

- Rename the builtin registry entry from `bool` to `boolean`.
- Migrate every maintained source-level type annotation in `lib/`.
- Update the type-naming authority.
- Add resolver coverage proving `boolean` denotes `Types::bool()` and `bool` is rejected, including the resource arity diagnostic witness.

## Acceptance

`boolean` resolves to the existing boolean `Ty`; `bool` does not resolve as a builtin; the maintained runtime library compiles with the canonical spelling; focused resolver tests and the relevant library/fixture gates pass.

## Non-goals

Rust’s internal `bool` identifiers and runtime/telemetry tags remain implementation details, not source-language spelling.

comments.text:
Delivered in 783250dcc. `boolean` is now the source-level builtin and extern wire spelling; maintained Fz library annotations and the type-naming authority use it. The resolver and extern-contract tests prove the canonical spelling; the explicit `bool`-rejection test was removed by request.

Validated: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --all-features (2088 compiler tests passed, 5 ignored; 708 fixture trials; 30 CLI; 266 runtime; metadata and doctests).

title: Align the boolean type constructor with Elixir
